description: The Propensity to Cycle Tool is an open-source planning support system that estimates cycling potential and its health and carbon benefits across England and Wales. It models where people could cycle under scenarios such as the Department for Transport's target to double cycling and a Go Dutch scenario reaching Dutch cycling levels while allowing for English and Welsh hilliness and trip distances, for a commuting layer and a school travel layer, at the level of areas, desire lines and routes on the road network. It was developed by researchers at Cambridge (CEDAR), LSHTM, Leeds and Westminster with funding from the Department for Transport (2015 to 2017 and 2018 to 2019) and the Welsh Government; methods are in Lovelace et al. (2017, Journal of Transport and Land Use) and Goodman et al. (2019, Journal of Transport and Health). The web tool is free, area and route data download as CSV or GeoJSON, manuals and R training material are provided, and the code on GitHub (npct) is licensed AGPL-3.0. Caveats: coverage is limited to England and Wales, scenarios are based on commuting and school travel, not all trips, and the training material dates from 2016 to 2019. The PCT supports capacity planning and network design of cycle infrastructure and prioritisation of routes; its route layer builds on cycle routing data from CycleStreets, and the companion pct R package gives programmatic access to its data.
